patients.label: Low risk, complete data
patients.purpose: Baseline healthy-ish case. Confirms the UI shows a calm/reassuring state, not just red urgency. Use this to test that low-risk styling actually looks distinct from high-risk.

patients.label: Moderate risk, complete data
patients.purpose: Middle-of-the-scale case. Tests that Moderate/Yellow states render distinctly from both Low/Green and High/Red — the state most UIs under-design.

patients.label: High risk, complete data (multi-condition)
patients.purpose: Your existing TETRA010 demo case — Stage 2 HTN + high IDRS + CKD G2/A2. Keep as the headline demo patient since it's already verified working end-to-end.

patients.label: Moderate risk, missing cholesterol + creatinine
patients.purpose: Core 'graceful degradation' demo case. No cholesterol → engine must fall back to non-lab WHO-CVD chart using BMI. No creatinine → CKD engine must flag missing investigation instead of guessing. This is the single most important case for judges — run it live.

expected.who_cvd_band: computed via non-lab/BMI chart, not lab chart
expected.kdigo_color: not computable — must return 'missing: serum creatinine, urine ACR' rather than defaulting
expected.referral: depends on ASCVD proxy; primary demo value is the missing-investigation flags, not the referral outcome

patients.label: Minimal data — vitals only, no labs at all
patients.purpose: Extreme graceful-degradation case for a rural screening-camp scenario. Only demographics + BP + waist circumference available — no cholesterol, no creatinine, no ACR. Tests that every module still returns a usable partial result plus a clear missing-tests list, and doesn't crash or silently substitute defaults.

expected.who_cvd_band: not computable — neither cholesterol nor BMI available; must return explicit 'insufficient data, recommend BMI or lipid panel' rather than guessing
expected.kdigo_color: not computable — recommend serum creatinine + ACR
expected.referral: IDRS high risk alone should be enough to trigger a referral/monitor recommendation even with everything else missing

patients.label: Fully normal / healthy, complete data
patients.purpose: Negative control. Every score should land in the lowest risk band. Important for demo credibility — shows the system doesn't just alarm on everyone.

expected.referral: not recommended — routine reassessment in 1 year

patients.label: Severe multi-comorbidity — Stage 2 HTN + advanced CKD + high CVD
patients.purpose: Stress-tests the cross-module rules from 2017_ACC_AHA.txt: strict BP goal <130/80 for CKD+HTN overlap, ACE-inhibitor-first recommendation, and the 'red/very high' KDIGO band. Good second demo case to show the system handles complexity, not just single-condition cases.

expected.idrs_category: high (already diagnosed — should not re-flag as 'needs referral for diagnosis', should route to management guidance instead)
expected.who_cvd_band: 20-30% or higher — known clinical CVD present
expected.kdigo_color: red (G3b/G4 range eGFR with A3 albuminuria)
expected.referral: recommended — should surface the strict <130/80 BP goal and ACE-inhibitor-first note from the CKD+HTN cross-module rule

patients.label: Already-diagnosed diabetic — tests referral logic doesn't double-flag
patients.purpose: Checks that 'known_diabetes_diagnosis: yes' correctly changes the missing-investigation and referral messaging (should not say 'refer for OGTT to confirm diagnosis' for someone already diagnosed — should shift to management/monitoring language instead).

expected.idrs_category: high, but messaging should reflect known diagnosis rather than 'get tested'
expected.referral: should follow diabetes+HTN cross-module BP goal <130/80, thiazide/ACEi/ARB/CCB first-line note

patients.label: Acute ischemic stroke presentation — tests the acute protocol branch
patients.purpose: This is the test coverage gap your agent flagged earlier (acute stroke branches undertested). Use this to explicitly exercise the tPA-eligible BP threshold logic (<185/110 before, <180/105 after) from 2017_ACC_AHA.txt.

expected.note: This case should route through the acute stroke protocol, not the standard chronic HTN treatment-decision logic. Output should reference the <185/110 pre-tPA threshold explicitly.
expected.referral: immediate/emergent — acute presentation, not a routine referral

patients.label: Elderly, boundary/edge values — tests chart lookup edges
patients.purpose: Deliberately uses boundary values to test lookup-table edge handling: age exactly at a WHO chart band edge (70), BMI in the 34-35 range (the exact bug you already fixed), and SBP at the >=180 top band. Good regression case to keep permanently in your test suite.

expected.who_cvd_band: should resolve cleanly via non-lab chart at BMI 30-35 band, age 70-74, SBP >=180 — this exact combination is what previously exposed the BMI gap bug
